text:
Toronto's best scoring chance of the night was a 4 percent wrist shot, and it was all they needed to take the lead 48 seconds in. William Nylander beat Jakub Dobes from a low-danger spot, and then the Maple Leafs spent the rest of the game being outchanced. Montreal finished with 3.48 expected goals to Toronto's 2.57 and held the edge in every period, which makes the 3-2 result look about right on the ice even though a replay of every shot would give Toronto the win 55 percent of the time.

The gap is partly a power-play story. Neither side scored with the man advantage (0 for 2 for MTL, 0 for 3 for TOR), but the even-strength numbers were nearly level at 1.91 to 1.82, so Montreal's edge came from the extra minutes of pressure and a tighter finish. Josh Anderson tied it in the first with a 36 percent bat-down chance, Zachary Bolduc made it 2-1 early in the second, and Alexandre Carrier put the game out of reach at 13:12 of the third with a wrist shot that had only a 1 percent chance of going in.

Sergei Bobrovsky allowed 0.71 more goals than expected on 24 shots against, while Dobes stopped 0.57 more than expected. Nylander made it interesting with his second goal at 15:46, set up by Easton Cowan and John Tavares, but Toronto never found the equalizer. Carrier, Nylander and Anderson took the three stars.
